candidates.lead: Andrew Kowalczyk had lived in a tower block in Rochdale for 27 years and now calls a bungalow home
candidates.evidence_text: 'I didn't want to move from Seven Sisters flats - but now I'm delighted' - BBC News Image caption, Andrew Kowalczyk lived on the College Bank estate for 27 years but says he is now happy in his new home By Richard Stead North West Published 1 hour ago After 27 years living in the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale, Andrew Kowalczyk did not want to leave. But he said he felt the demolition of the flats, which have dominated the town's skyline since the 1960s, was "inevitable" and he was now relieved to have been rehoused. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) announced last week that the blocks would be bulldozed and replaced with a new College Bank estate of about 600 homes. It comes after a 10-year campaign by residents who wanted the flats to be refurbished and not knocked down but RBH said the demolition was the only "realistic" option. Kowalczyk, 61, who lived in the Mardyke block, said he was reluctant to move out of his "secure" home and the "great views" but he has since been rehomed in a bungalow in Lower Falinge and was now "delighted with it". Residents started to move out of the flats in October last year after long-term safety concerns were raised in October last year. The blocks are almost all empty, with 78 homes out of 766 currently occupied. Some of the remaining tenants have vowed to challenge the demolition decision. But Kowalczyk said: "I didn't want to move from College Bank because you had great views and your home was secure but I knew that - no matter how much we resisted - demolition is bound to happen. "When I looked at my new bungalow in Lower Falinge, it was really clean, there were new tiles, it also had new cupboards, so I made my mind up about moving in really quickly and now I'm delighted with it." Image source, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Image caption, The new College Bank estate is intended to have green spaces between Lower Falinge and the River Roch. Plans for the new £216m College Bank estate include a mix of mid-rise flats and houses, including family homes with three and four bedrooms. Amanda Newton, chief executive of RBH, said: "It will be a really modern, high quality new skyline for Rochdale. "The homes that are on College Bank now would only last for a maximum of 50 years - even if they were refurbished - so what we're doing now is creating homes that will last for almost double that - for the generations of the future". RBH said the new estate would have about 250 extra bed spaces, when compared to the number within the Seven Sisters towers. Image caption, Amanda Newton says the new estate will be a "modern" skyline The housing association said a refurbishment of the blocks would have taken 12 years and cost £269m, plus VAT. Any refurbishment would have been "extremely complex" and involve adding a second staircase, it said. But that is disputed by residents on the College Bank estate, who say any refurbishment would not need to be so expensive. Mark Slater, chair of the Campaign to Save the Seven Sisters, said: "Other 1960s tower blocks have been refurbished and they don't need a second staircase." Image source, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Image caption, The new College Bank estate would have around 600 homes - including three and four bedroom houses. Ten years ago, about a thousand people lived in the blocks but one of the buildings - Mitchell Hey - is now empty, and only 78 of the flats remain occupied. Salma Ashiq, who has moved from College Bank into a one-bedroom bungalow on the Lower Falinge estate in the last few weeks, said: "I was really anxious about moving because of all the stress, the waiting and the decorating, the building of the new furniture, so the anxiety for me was horrendous." "This new place is great - I had a vision of what I wanted and I think I've got everything," the 47 year-old added. Image caption, Salma Ashiq has moved from College Bank into a bungalow on the Lower Falinge estate. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing first proposed demolishing four of the Seven Sisters tower blocks in 2017 and there followed years of uncertainty. In 2024, Rochdale Council - and the town's MP Paul Waugh - backed calls for the Seven Sisters tower blocks to be protected from demolition. A College Bank Task Force, including RBH, Rochdale Council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority was later set up to examine the options. candidates.evidence_text: Families cannot return home after explosives found - BBC News Image caption, Police evacuated homes on Shelley Grove in Droylsden on Wednesday afternoon By Dan Wareing North West Published 20 November 2026 People are not expected to be able to return to their homes while police continue a search of a house where explosives were discovered. A bomb disposal unit was sent to Shelley Grove in Droylsden, Tameside, on Wednesday after the discovery made during an "unrelated investigation". A man in his 70s and a woman in her 60s were arrested on suspicion of unlawfully possessing ammunition and explosive substances, and a 20-year-old man was held on criminal damage, arson and possession of ammunition. They have all since been bailed. Greater Manchester Police said searches would continue over the weekend, and that people living within the cordon were "unable to return to their homes". candidates.evidence_text: Funeral plans being made in the Salford baby remains case - BBC News Image source, GMP Image caption, Baby Ava's remains were discovered by a dog walker in November 2024 By Dan Wareing North West Published 20 November 2026 Police say they are determined to get justice for a baby whose remains were found two years ago. The infant, named Ava by Greater Manchester Police, was discovered by a dog walker near Ashtons Field, in Little Hulton, Salford, on 20 November 2024. Despite a long-running investigation and a £50,000 reward put up by the Greater Manchester combined authority, detectives have still not been able to identify the child's mother. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said its determination to find the answers "has never wavered", and that it wanted to "secure the justice that Ava deserves". Det Insp Louise Kelly said: "We know 20 November will be particularly significant for Ava's parents, family members, and anyone who may have known her." She added: "Behind every line of enquiry, every review of evidence, and every piece of information we assess is a baby girl who will never be forgotten." Kelly said the force was currently trying to organise a funeral for Ava. She added: "We continue to consider and explore all investigative opportunities available to us. However, at this stage we still do not have answers." She said clothing that was found at the scene had provided "no new viable leads". candidates.evidence_text: Cheetham Hill Big plans for old Cheetham Hill GRUB plot as CGIs show how site could be transformed Two towers of 18 and 43 storeys would contain more than 500 homes Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 0 Plans for two new tower blocks - with more than 500 new homes - in north Manchester have been submitted to the council An application has been lodged for the development at 50-54 Red Bank, close to the Green Quarter and Cheetham Hill . It could transform the skyline in the corner of the city The scheme, by LWP Redbank Ltd, would see two residential buildings of 18 and 43 storeys built on the plot, previously occupied by food and drink venue GRUB Designed by Jon Matthews Architects, the towers would contain 509 one, two and three-bedroom flats, as well as commercial space on the ground floor. A witness heard him say: "I think I passed out driving the car - it's crashed." The 26-year-old lost control of his adapted vehicle - which had sports seats and an injection system to give his engine more power - before crashed into a digger and a dumper truck at a set of roadworks, ending up on a wall Simms' two rear seat passengers - one of them his girlfriend - suffered fatal head and neck injuries in the crash on the A57 Hyde Road in Gorton on August 5 earlier this year. Natasha Denman, 24, and Jack Cartwright, 23, died at the scene On Friday (November 20), a judge jailed Simms, from Longsight. Manchester Crown Court heard he spewed up bright blue vomit in the back of an ambulance following the horror crash, admitting he had been drinking BuzzBallz. A bottle was found almost empty in the footwell of the Skod

But her remains were found on Wednesday November 20th 2024 on top of a snow-covered field It is believed a badger, fox, or large bird hunting for food in freezing conditions brought her tiny body to the surface a day or hours after it was left there. Ava was found by a dog being walked at Ashtons Field, Little Hulton, Salford Intensive work by scientists and police mean they can be certain as to the 20-day period in which Baby Ava was left at the entrance to the country park, created on the site of a former colliery. An estimated 600 people took part in the demonstration, one of a number of similar events held across the country, under the banner of 'In Demonstrators called for an end to war and the 'militarisation of education' as they gathered underneath the Whitworth Arch, at the University of Manchester on Oxford Road, at midday They then marched down Oxford Road towards St Peter’s Square where a further rally was held. In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.” District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour Semenyo, who was a Bournemouth player at the time of the incident, but is now signed for Manchester City, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mr Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

candidates.evidence_text: Revive Skin & Hair wins Altrincham's Winter Windows competition – now vote for your favourite Skip to content News — Shops Revive Skin & Hair wins Altrincham's Winter Windows competition – now vote for your favourite A total of 36 shops and businesses have taken part this year. , and David Prior November 20, 2026 . 3:06 PM 2 min read Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Revive Skin & Hair has been judged the winner of Altrincham's annual Winter Windows competition Revive Skin & Hair has been crowned the winner of Altrincham's annual Winter Windows competition with a festive display featuring beautifully illustrated Christmas carol characters. Last year's winner, Heritage Healthcare in Goose Green, was a close second with its Nutcracker-themed window. A total of 36 shops and businesses have taken part in this year's competition, which is organised by Altrincham BID, the team behind Visit Altrincham. This year's judges were Maria Bota, Director of Cultural Transformation at Trafford Council, and Bronte James, the council's Culture Support Officer, who toured the town to assess the entries. They said: "The standard was incredibly high, and it was wonderful to see the imagination, creativity and effort that Altrincham's businesses and retailers have put into their displays. Heritage Healthcare, in Goose Green, was a close second with its Nutcracker-themed window "Each window brought something different to the town, and we loved seeing the individuality, attention to detail and festive spirit on display." Of the winning entry, they added: "The intricate detail and creativity, with the artwork filling the entire window, made for a wonderfully engaging display that really caught the eye." There was a special mention for Altytude, the town's new independent gym, whose 80s-inspired window was a nod to the theme of tomorrow's Christmas Lights Switch-On. Nando's, Love Bridal and MOST Bakery also received special mentions for their displays. Mandy White, Altrincham BID Director, said: "Altrincham is a fantastic place to celebrate the festive season. With the renowned Altrincham Market and Market House, an incredible selection of independent shops and popular high-street brands, the town has something for everyone. This year's judges were Trafford Council's Maria Bota (second from left) and Bronte James (far left), with Altrincham BID's Mandy White and Sam from Share Your Story "Our diverse range of restaurants, coffee shops and bars makes Altrincham the perfect festive destination, and the effort our businesses put into the Winter Windows Competition adds so much to the atmosphere of the town. It's wonderful to see so many businesses getting involved and bringing a little extra magic to our streets." She also thanked the judges and Share Your Story for photographing this year's entries. 🗳️ Vote for your favourite Winter Window! The judges have had their say – now it's your turn! Which of Altrincham's 36 festive windows deserves to win this year's People's Choice Award? How to vote: Head over to the Altrincham Today Facebook page. Find our Winter Windows 2026 photo gallery. Simply 'like' the photograph of your favourite window. Alternatively, you can vote through the Visit Altrincham app. Every vote counts and the winner will be announced next week! candidates.title: Blow for Timperley traders as bid to halt parking charges is defeated
candidates.summary: The proposed parking changes are expected to take effect in summer 2027
candidates.reason: Semantic borderline kept: Голосование состоялось: поправка против платной парковки отклонена, ввод с лета 2027 | Selection: Selected in last_24h shortlist before writing.

candidates.lead: The proposed parking changes are expected to take effect in summer 2027
candidates.evidence_text: Blow for Timperley traders as bid to halt parking charges is defeated Skip to content News — Council Blow for Timperley traders as bid to halt parking charges is defeated The proposed parking changes are expected to take effect in summer 2027. , and David Prior November 20, 2026 . 10:07 AM 2 min read Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford councillors have rejected calls to scrap planned parking charges in Timperley and the proposed introduction of evening and Sunday charges across the borough. At Wednesday night’s Full Council meeting, a Conservative amendment calling for the proposals to be withdrawn was defeated, while a Labour amendment removing opposition to the extension of parking charges was passed. The original Liberal Democrat motion, tabled by Timperley North councillor Jane Brophy, had warned that extending charges to smaller district centres risked damaging businesses already facing significant pressures. Labour’s successful amendment removed that commitment, replacing it with a statement that “Parking charges should reflect the different needs and offers in areas across Trafford.” The vote does not, however, mean the proposed charges have been formally approved. As previously reported by Altrincham Today , Trafford Council is looking to generate an additional £250,000 a year from parking as part of its draft 2027/28 budget. The proposals include introducing charges at the currently free Thorley Lane car park in Timperley and extending charging hours elsewhere. Speaking during the debate, Liberal Democrat group leader Cllr Shaun Ennis said: “I've spoken to every single business in Timperley Village and it is absolutely clear that these charges will be a slap in the face for small business owners trying to operate in extremely challenging times.” Conservative Hale councillor Rupert Kelly, who moved his group’s amendment, also questioned the impact on local businesses. “Why would anyone pay to park in Timperley village whilst the local supermarkets and the Trafford centre are free?” he said. “You cannot regenerate a high street by charging people for the privilege of visiting it.” Deputy council leader Cllr Liz Patel defended the proposals, saying: “There is currently a live consultation on this, and charges proposed there would bring it in line with other village centres.” She added: “We don't set our budget via motions.” Cllr Brophy said the Liberal Democrats would vote against their own motion if Labour’s amendment was successful because it would remove one of its central commitments. The amended motion was subsequently carried. The proposed parking changes are expected to take effect in summer 2027, subject to the necessary approvals. Precise tariffs and a full list of affected locations have yet to be published. Trafford’s final budget is due to be agreed at a Full Council meeting on February 24th. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The debate follows widespread criticism of plans to introduce charges at the currently free Thorley Lane car park Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Controversial plans to introduce parking charges in Timperley village will come under renewed scrutiny tonight as Trafford councillors debate a motion opposing the extension of charges across the borough's district centres The Liberal Democrats are calling on the council to oppose the extension of charging, while the Conservatives have submitted an amendment calling for the proposed new charges to be withdrawn altogether The debate follows widespread criticism of plans to introduce charges at the currently free Thorley Lane car park in Timperley As reported by Altrincham Today last month , local councillors have warned that the proposals could damage independent businesses, drive shoppers to neighbouring areas offering free parking and push motorists into surrounding residential streets Timperley councillors Julian Newgrosh and Shaun Ennis told October's Executive meeting that there was widespread opposition to the plans within the village

candidates.evidence_text: Winners of this year's prestigious Manchester Culture Awards were announced at the weekend with cultural organisations big and small from across the city recognised, along with creatives and participants ranging in age from 19 to 90! Launched by the city council back in 2018 to acknowledge Manchester's fast-growing reputation for culture and the arts, the annual awards recognise the very best of culture, creativity and arts in the city - from the grassroots up Nominations for the awards were invited across eleven different categories from members of the public, arts professionals, the voluntary sector and anyone else with an interest in the arts Over 400 nominations were received across the different award categories with awards up for grabs including Young Creative of the Year - which this year went to Demereece Green, a young creative from Harpurhey who through his work has created a safe space for young people to expl In a ceremony hosted by Manchester-based composer, DJ, broadcaster, and cultural leader AFRODEUTSCHE, other gongs on the night went to The Royal Exchange Theatre for their bold revival of Jim Cartwright's Road which won Best Performance; to Z-arts for their fully immersive Advent The evening also saw awards made across categories that shine a spotlight on important themes of our time such as health and wellbeing, equality and social justice, and climate change - with Factory International and The Walk Productions winning the Our Planet: Acting on Climate

Visitors can also enjoy value-for-money funfair rides, with 95% The events have been planned to cater for a wide audience, including those who would prefer to attend an earlier, shorter, lower-noise display. Avoidable single-use plastics have been removed from all event sites, the pyrotechnics supplier uses sustainable packaging, and post-event litter picks will take place immediately after the celebrations. candidates.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . Ten years after it last played to audiences in its original home of London and the UK, this landmark production returns at last. Wor Billy! What a sensation, what an inspiration. Billy is a slice of British life that speaks to everyone Set in a northern town during the miners’ strike of 1984/85, the show follows Billy’s journey from the boxing ring to the ballet class, where he discovers a passion for dance that will change his life forever. As Billy dares to dream, his courage unites his family, inspires his community, and proves the transformative power of art. Brought to life by the award-winning creative team behind the film, with iconic music by Elton John, Billy Elliot the Musical is an extraordinary theatrical experience that has captivated audiences around the world. A dazzling 40-carat gem of a show Billy boy, this is the greatest musical yet Truly electrifying – this heart-stopping show is a must-see Buy direct from venues with ATG Tickets. Transparent booking fees, no late stage surprises. Palace Theatre Manchester The Palace Theatre of Varieties opened on Whit Monday 1891 and cost its owners the then colossal sum of £40,500. In the late 1970’s the Palace Theatre underwent a major refurbishment and re-opened in 1981 with Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Jesus Christ Superstar and has since then retained its position as the premier provincial touring venue

Taking over Contact on Saturday 21 November, the festival pairs films by emerging Two of the highlights come from SEE MY WORLD itself. Homage brings together dancers, teachers and ballroom performers with archive footage from Hulme and Moss Side to tell a story of Manchester through the people who’ve kept it dancing. In Poetic Justice , director Daniel Oyegade Elsewhere, Darshan Gajjar steps back inside the shop where his grandfather rebuilt his life after leaving Uganda in SHOP DADA: The Cornershop That Built Us . Asma Kabadeh’s A Story Left Behind follows a researcher piecing together the life of Sheffield’s first documented Somali w The thread running through the programme is Sasa na Zamani , an idea explored by Kenyan philosopher John Mbiti about how the past shapes the present. One place to see that up close is the Ahmed Iqbal Ullah RACE Centre’s archive display. Founder and resident DJ Beatnix Nicole grew up around the legendary Keele All-nighters, which were run by her family. She started the night as an opportunity to DJ alongside her dad, ‘Keele’ Neil Clowes, an For the winter edition, Gary Bratchford of Home Run Soul Club goes back-to-back with Blackbee Soul Club’s Sam McEwan, while Burnin’ Up Soul Club’s Maggy Grooves and Jake Fairham make a welcome return Fresh from the Munich Soul Weekender, Beatnix Nicole and Luci Jones will be digging into their collections of rare soul 45s, with Keele Neil Clowes serving up a selection of classic Northern Soul

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. candidates.evidence_text: Clint Boon spinning records on Greek Street on a Saturday afternoon, and it won’t cost you a penny. Stopford Park is throwing a free party to launch Bosden, the first of its new apartment buildings, just up from the Town Hall Clint Boon needs very little introduction round these parts. The Inspiral Carpets man was right in the middle of Madchester and he’s still at it, touring and recently publishing his book, The Manchester Chronicles . He’ll be sharing the decks with DJ, presenter and podcaster Matt There’ll be a talk from John Barratt, co-founder of the Stockport Music Story with his wife Rosemary. John founded the record label Facsimile Liaisons which took him to Strawberry Studios, he’s worked with Easterhouse and Syncopation, and also signed The Family Foundation, Ultrac There will be a pop-up from I Knead Pizza, and it’s also the first chance to have a nosey round the show apartment at Bosden with the remaining apartments going on the market the same day. If you’re tempted to have a look round you can register your interest here Make a weekend of it: Foodie Friday is on across the Market Place and Great Underbank the night before, from 6pm

candidates.lead: Micro Commercial Components (MCC), a leading manufacturer of discrete semiconductors headquartered in California, USA, has chosen Manchester Science Park (MSP) as the location for its first European Research & Development facility.
candidates.evidence_text: Micro Commercial Components opens new semiconductor design centre in Manchester - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Advanced materials & manufacturing Micro Commercial Components opens new semiconductor design centre in Manchester Published on November 19, 2026 News Micro Commercial Components (MCC), a leading manufacturer of discrete semiconductors headquartered in California, USA, has chosen Manchester Science Park (MSP) as the location for its first European Research & Development facility. The engineers will focus on the design of leading-edge power MOSFETs, devices critical to improving energy efficiency in power-hungry applications such as AI datacentres, robotics and electric vehicles. MCC intends to increase the current team of 8 to around 30 over the next couple of years. Manchester Science Park is experienced in supporting fast-growing organisations and provides a flexible environment that can accommodate this type of expansion. Chris Boyce, General Manager, R&D of the new venture, commented : “We looked at a number of locations across the UK and beyond, but the Manchester proposition in general, and at MSP in particular, was just too compelling in terms of a pro-growth business regime and excellent links to the local universities.” Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig, said: “Greater Manchester is the fastest growing city region in the UK, and we’re on a mission to bring good jobs to our region that benefit local people in every bit of Greater Manchester. “We’re proud to welcome MCC to Greater Manchester as the company opens its first European research and development centre at Manchester Science Park. “MCC’s decision to grow its team here, scaling up to 30 engineering roles over the next couple of years, is a vote of confidence in our talent, our universities and the strength of our city region’s advanced manufacturing and technology sectors.” The whole deal was pulled together by Invest Manchester. Joe Manning, Managing Director of Invest Manchester, said : “It’s great to welcome investment from California semiconductor company MCC as it opens its first European R&D centre here in Manchester. This is a key sector for the city and at the heart of our AI and digital sector, which is worth £5bn to Greater Manchester. “MCC’s investment will create 30 high value jobs in Manchester Science Park, and we look forward to continuing to support the company as it expands here.” The centre was opened today by Cllr Garry Bridges, Leader of Manchester City Council, with MCC senior management and representatives of the local innovation ecosystem enjoying technology demonstrations and a tour of the facility. Cllr Bridges, said : “Micro Commercial Components’ choice of Manchester as its European research base reflects and reinforces Manchester’s growing reputation as a centre for leading edge research and development. “As well as supporting more highly-skilled jobs for the city, MCC’s engineers will add to the strength of the city’s technology and advanced manufacturing sectors by working closely with our universities and research institutions on the Oxford Road corridor. “We welcome MCC to the city and look forward to them flourishing here.” Similar Articles Graphene Innovations Manchester opens new advanced materials factory in Trafford Advanced materials & manufacturing Manchester’s industrial story has entered a new chapter. Drawing on Seva’s own encounters w Performed and choreographed by Seva, the work draws on hip hop and contemporary dance to excavate his own experiences of abandonment, faith and frustration, illuminating the ways in which these formative forces become embedded in the body and influence our sense of identity Rather than approaching memory as something fixed or safely consigned to the past, Sing Child Sing traces its patterns from childhood into maturity, informing our relationships, our instincts and the ways we navigate the world Seva has established himself as one of contemporary dance theatre’s most distinctive voices, with Far From The Norm earning an Olivier Award for BLKDOG . In his latest creation, sound, lighting and movement combine to create a shifting, immersive interior landscape in which past For all its intimately personal foundations, the production finds a universal resonance in exploring the experiences that shape us, and what it means to reclaim agency over the stories we inherit Sing Child Sing arrives at Lowry as part of the company’s ongoing relationship with the venue, where Far From The Norm is a partner company

Engels lived here, on and off, for 22 years, during which time Marx would stay with him for long periods. The remarkable tale of two men who changed the political world is told on thi In the 1840s, industrial Manchester appeared to confirm for both Engels and Marx the truth behind their ideas of how society was ordered and where it was inevitably headed. It seemed clear to them how the tensions between the ‘bourgeoisie’ and ‘proletariat’ would ultimately lead It would probably not have been clear to them that present commemorations in Greater Manchester would include a climbing wall in the shape of the face and beard of Engels Still, the fact they filtered their ideas as young men through the experience of Manchester was crucial. Many things we have done well but many we need to do better. It doesn’t change the way we analyse things “To be consistent is the main thing if you want to compete for something “We were consistent, but in the last three games, our performance was good in two of them but you have to be consistent [in all matches]

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Liverpool fan not guilty of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo after Man City star withdraws support A court heard the Manchester City player has withdrawn his support for the prosecution Add to preferred sources Comments News PA and Paul Britton A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing now Manchester City footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates’ Court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on August 15 last year But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: “Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him. In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.” District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour Semenyo, who was a Bournemouth player at the time of the incident, but is now signed for Manchester City, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mr Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure

candidates.evidence_text: Prefer the Guardian on Google 1. Moyes: ‘I want Jack to show more’ David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October but he is fit and available for Mon “He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before,” the Everton manager said. “We will get on with things. The team is doing really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.” The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week andalso apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who won three of four matches in his absence.
